stories.title: Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say
bullet_points: Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail     Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms     Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two  Florida   immigration  jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.

Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two  Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)  facilities in south Florida.

stories.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
bullet_points: Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda  Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.
The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola.
It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.

stories.title: RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau
bullet_points: Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns  Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials  said  on Facebook.

The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m.
Continue reading...

stories.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum
bullet_points: Result is a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity  Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement.
With nearly 1.9m votes counted, roughly 76% people supported remaining in Canada, while 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.
